items.note: The filter field has typed text with an ink border and a flush pink halo, as the input focus recipe says. The table above it shrinks to the one matching row, and the count reads 'Showing 1 of 8'. The teal band stays the only band color, and the pink halo is the only pink in view.

On the black ground the focused filter field keeps a light-pink halo around a raised field, and the filtered single row and its count are readable. The Refresh button flips to paper-filled, as the dark mapping says.

The stacked layout ends in the filter field, which has an ink border and a pink halo. Below it is the one-row result table. The focus treatment matches desktop, and nothing in the state is hidden or overlaps.

The first table row has a flat subtle-gray fill with no lift. Its row-action arrow keeps the small outlined icon box, which follows the table-row hover rule. Status pills read as outlined icon-plus-word badges.

The hovered first row is only a slightly lighter charcoal than the rows below. That is faint but visible, and no worse than the earlier version, which earlier verdicts already noted. The rest of the table (ink rules, outlined status pills, row-action boxes) maps cleanly to dark.

On mobile the first row has the gray hover fill across the bordered table box. Project names wrap to two lines, and the status pills stay in their own column. Nothing lifts, which follows the 'no lift on whole rows' rule.

Keyboard focus is on the 'Projects' nav pill, shown as a 2px ink ring that follows the pill's full radius. It sits just under the ink-filled current-page pill, so focus and current page are clearly different.
In dark the focused 'Projects' pill gets a pink ring around a pill shape, under the paper-filled current-page pill. The ring is easy to see on black and doesn't fill the pill.
In the mobile top pill strip, 'Projects' has an ink focus ring next to the ink-filled 'Overview' current pill. It is the same focus treatment as desktop, at touch size.

The account menu opens as a raised panel with an ink border and a hard offset shadow, holding the email, Account settings, My team and Sign out. The trigger turns solid pink while the menu is open, though the spec now explicitly says open menu triggers are never pink.
In dark the menu panel is charcoal with a light ink border and an offset shadow, but the open trigger is again filled pink.
On mobile the menu panel drops over the teal band and covers part of the 'Overview' title, which is acceptable for an open overlay. The avatar trigger beside the search is filled pink while open.

Under the filter field, which shows a pink halo, the table is replaced by an outlined empty panel. It has a small sticker, 'No projects match your filters', a hint line and one pink 'Clear filters' button. Refresh is now ink, so the pink action that earlier verdicts flagged as doubled is now the only one.

The dark empty panel is charcoal with the same sticker, message and pink 'Clear filters' button. The band's Refresh button is paper-filled, so only one pink action is visible and the next step is clear.
On mobile the empty panel stacks the sticker, a two-line heading, the hint and a pink 'Clear filters' button under the focused filter field. The band's Refresh is ink, so one pink action is in view.

Each stat card is replaced by a small pink loading coin and 'Loading...', which follows the coin-instead-of-spinner rule. On the teal band, though, the 'Refreshing...' button is gray text on a light-gray fill with no ink border, so it reads washed out against the band.
In dark the four stat cards each show a pink coin and 'Loading...' on charcoal. The 'Refreshing...' button is a dark fill with light text and a small coin, which stays readable on the teal band.
The four stacked stat cards each show a loading coin with 'Loading...'. The band's 'Refreshing...' button has the same low-contrast gray-on-gray disabled look as on desktop light.

findings.summary: The account menu's trigger still fills solid pink while its menu is open, in light, dark and mobile. Earlier verdicts already flagged this, and the spec now says outright that open menu triggers use the raised or ink fill, never pink.
findings.promptFix: Put the open/expanded state of any menu, select or disclosure trigger (aria-expanded="true") in the Interaction table and in the trigger component itself: color.surface.raised fill with the ink border, or color.action.inverse for a solid trigger. Never color.action.primary. Add a Verification step: open every menu and check that no trigger turned pink.

findings.summary: In light mode the disabled 'Refreshing...' button on the color band is gray text on a pale-gray fill with no ink border. It looks washed out and low-contrast against the band, which goes against the spec's 'no disabled-looking text on a band' and 4.5:1 rules. Dark mode keeps it readable.
